newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan thirst for Middle East oil still growing.
newsitem.headline: Japan thirst for Middle East oil still growing.

text.p: Japan's thirst for Middle East oil is still growing, and growing fast, according to trade ministry statistics.
But the trend is more an industry strategy than a cause of concern, according to Japanese oil traders.

May import data released on Tuesday reveals that Japan's year-to-date crude oil purchases from the Middle East now represent nearly 82.8 percent of the country's 4.8-million barrel-per-day crude oil imports, up from 80.1 percent for the same period in 1996 and 78.2 percent in 1995.
"Of course there is an underlying concern over stability in the Middle East, but that concern is no longer paramount," said Isao Kusakabe, manager of Cosmo Oil Co Ltd's crude trading unit.

Traders say a growing level of sophistication within Japan's refining sector -- especially new desulphurisation units which allow refiners to produce cleaner, higher quality products from lower quality crude grades -- has allowed them to bargain shop for more of the Middle East's relatively heavy, high-sulphur grades.
Concerns over Middle East stability, traders say, can be assuaged by diversifying suppliers within the highly volatile but richly endowed region, rather than outside of it.
"It's important to remember that there are many countries in the Middle East," said Cosmo's Kusakabe.
"While it is true that they reside very close together in a political hotspot, we try to maintain good enough relations with enough of them to spread the risk," he said.
So far in 1997, Japan has imported from the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Qatar, Kuwait, the Neutral Zone, Oman, Iraq, and Yemen, in descending order by volume.
Traders also say the growing reliance highlights Japan's priority of contracting supplies over a specified period of time rather than resorting to global spot markets.

"The Persian Gulf grades tend to be purchased on a term basis, which makes them reliable in the short-term but politically difficult to reduce," said John Popham, vice president of oil trader East-West Energy Ltd in Tokyo.

Year-to-date import statistics show that Japan purchased some 15.8 percent of its crude oil from regional suppliers in Asia and Australia, which represents a fall of 1.8 percentage points from 1996 levels of 17.6 percent and 3.6 percentage points from 1995 levels of 19.4 percent.
Year-to-date purchases from West African and Latin American sources were 1.1 percent and 0.3 percent of the total, respectively.
